reviews.title: Ruined By Rebrand
reviews.text:
MoneyWalk was a great app! It was legitimate and I made some pocket change off of it because I walk so much for work. However, this AHEALTH rebrand ruined EVERY SINGLE REDEEMABLE QUALITY MoneyWalk had. 

First, it’s now painfully health-based and has this very off-putting obsession with de-aging, using elements like taking time off of an app-implemented “bio age”. Previously, we’ve all had the silent agreement that apps like this sold our location data and served us ads in exchange for a little cash. It wasn’t a broken system, so why fix it????

Lastly, my biggest gripe with AHEALTH is that it absolutely ruined the coin system and made it borderline impossible to see a future payout of $5 in anywhere close to a reasonable amount of time. For example, I walked 8k steps today! Moneywalk would’ve given me 100 coins, and then randomized extras for each milestone from 1k-5k? Usually ranging from 20-60 coins. AHEALTH gave me 32 coins, and its equivalent to the milestone feature gave me a measly 10-15.

I ask again to the dev team and ownership: this app was NOT BROKEN. Why did you make it not even worth using, and disguised this change as a “fix”?

In short: I’m switching to a competitor app that doesn’t pull moves like this. You should, too!

reviews.title: Unsolicited and Incorrect Health Advice
reviews.text: I’ve had this app for a few months and it is getting more and more updates. It’s not about walking anymore, it’s about improving “bio age” which is fine, I suppose. You can get additional points for other things, including entering your “diet.” As a dietitian, I explicitly put in extremely vague food information, this app has nothing to do with food. The current update now gives AI generated dietary advice that is very harmful and again, out of the scope for this app. I entered an objectively  healthy meal and it told me it was “good” and could use improvements. The information said kale is high in carbohydrates, watermelon was too high in sugar, peanuts were not a good enough protein source, etc. This is why people have eating disorders, apps like this with no business in giving dietary advice. Please get rid of this nonsense and do not tell users food is healthy or unhealthy. The point of your app is to get rewards for healthy behaviors, not provide shameful and unnecessary comments about what someone eats. This is shameful on your part.
